$comment: Golden cases for the Foundation Model connector's GROUNDED slice: the case
supplies the rows (groundedData), the model must narrate them, and truth is
the supplied value itself (`expected`) - reference SQL would prove nothing
the rows don't already prove, and needs no warehouse. What IS under test:
the FM path forwards groundedData, the narration cites the right figure
(reconcile), invents no others (grounding gate), and obeys the Roman-scale
notation convention. This is the eval for 'retrieve then narrate' - the
ungrounded FM failure mode is confidently citing numbers nobody supplied.
Values mirror the synthetic SCM star's documented reconciled figures
(docs/synthetic_poc/PBI_APPLES_TO_APPLES.md) so a human reading a transcript
recognizes them, but the eval holds for ANY values - the rows are the truth
No truthProfile on purpose: these cases must run with zero warehouse access.

cases.question: In two sentences, summarize on-time delivery performance for 2026 year to date, citing the OTIF percentage.
cases.why: The basic faithful-citation case: one rate to cite, two decoys beside it. Reconcile checks the cited OTIF; the grounding gate checks the decoys weren't garbled into new numbers.

cases.question: State net sales for 2025 in one sentence, citing the exact figure.
cases.why: Billion-scale currency: the narration must land at 1.88B, and the notation gate rejects the K/M-for-million habits that misstate it by three orders of magnitude.

cases.question: Describe the GHG emissions trend across these years in two sentences, citing the 2026 year-to-date figure.
cases.why: A declining series where the model must pick the RIGHT year's value to cite - trend prose loves to cite the biggest number instead.

cases.question: In one sentence, state the gross margin percentage for 2026 year to date.
cases.why: A percent under 100 next to percents of similar size (55.60 vs 55.23 vs 53.84): tolerance is tightened so citing an adjacent year fails rather than squeaking by.

cases.question: Compare the Order Fill Rate between 2024 and 2026 year to date in two sentences, citing both percentages.
cases.why: Two required citations in one answer. Reconcile anchors on the 2026 value; the grounding gate requires the 2024 figure to also come from the rows rather than being paraphrased into a new number.

cases.question: State total units produced for 2025 in one sentence, citing the exact figure.
cases.why: A mid-scale count (tens of millions) - the MM boundary case for the notation convention on narrated output.

cases.question: In one sentence, state the energy intensity in kWh per unit for 2025.
cases.why: A small ratio (single digits): no magnitude suffix applies, so this catches a model that reflexively scales everything.

cases.question: Write a two-sentence KPI snapshot for 2026 year to date from these figures, citing OTIF and net sales.
cases.why: The composite case closest to real product output: multiple measures of mixed kinds in one narration. Reconcile anchors on OTIF; grounding must hold across everything else cited.
